title: Cancer Elemental Risk Assessments in Hookah: Analysis of Traditional and Flavored Tobaccos
author: Nikbakhtan, Hassan, et al.
materials: We obtained five kinds of water pipe tobaccos that are commonly used in Iran from local shops. We used three types of tobaccos with flavors (Apple, Orange, and Blueberry) and two types of tobaccos with traditional names (Borazjan and Khansar) for this study. The chemicals, HNO3 70 %, and H2O2 30 %, were purchased from Sigma-Aldrich.

The Agilent 7900 ICP-MS with the octupole reaction system (ORS) collision/reaction cell (CRC) was used for the analysis of metal amounts in the digested samples. The ORS was operated in helium collision mode to remove all matrix-based polyatomic interferences. The technique covers the entire essential validation parameters concerning assessments on ICP-MS, including operating conditions, instrument multi-element calibration standards, sensitivity check, and reagent blank. all elements were measured using a single set of operating conditions without switching cell gas modes. The sample introduction system consisted of a Micro Mist glass concentric nebulizer and a quartz double-pass Scott-type spray chamber maintained at a temperature of 4 °C. A standard quartz torch with 2.5 mm internal diameter (ID) injector was used. auto-tuned using the 7900 Mass Hunter software. The instrument was equipped with an Agilent I-AS integrated autosampler. The instrumental parameters are given in Table 1. Ultra-pure water obtained from a Milli-Q purification device (Millipore Co., Bedford, MA, USA). Standard labware and glassware were acid washed and rinsed with Ultra-pure water. Multi-elemental standard solution for ICP-OES contains elements of Al, As, Ba, Bi, Ca, Cd, Ce, Hg, Mg, Na, P, Pb, Se, Sr, Tb, (10 ppm, 26XSM80B.5 L) and Multi-elemental standard solution for ICP-OES contains elements of B, Co, Cr, Cu, Fe, K, Li, Mn, Mo, Ni, Sb, Si, Sn, Ti, V, Zn, (10 ppm, 26XSM90C.5 L), was obtained from MBH, (London, England). The mixed standard solution was obtained by further diluted to desired concentration daily prior to use. steps.title: Collect samples and reagents
steps.instruction: Obtain five water‑pipe tobacco types commonly used in Iran: three flavored (Apple, Orange, Blueberry) and two traditional (Borazjan, Khansar). Purchase concentrated nitric acid (HNO₃, 70 %) and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂, 30 %) from Sigma‑Aldrich and keep all materials ready for analysis.

steps.title: Determine ash content
steps.instruction: Weigh 5.0 g of each tobacco sample into a crucible, place in a muffle furnace, heat at 600 °C for 2 h, then cool to obtain ash for later metal analysis.

steps.title: Digest tobacco and ash
steps.instruction: Perform acid digestion of each homogenized tobacco sample and its corresponding ash, as well as reagent blanks, before filtration and dilution.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 0.50 g of each homogenized tobacco sample and each ash into separate digestion vessels.
Prepare a reagent blank for each batch (10 vessels total) by adding Milli‑Q™ water instead of sample.
Add 5 mL concentrated HNO₃ (70 %) and 2 mL H₂O₂ (30 %) to every vessel.
Allow a pre‑digestion period of approximately 1 h at ambient temperature.
Seal the vessels and place them in a water bath set to 90 °C until digestion is complete.
After cooling, filter the upper liquid layer through a paper filter into acid‑washed polypropylene tubes.
Dilute the filtrate to a final volume of 25 mL with Milli‑Q™ water.
Store the tubes at 4–6 °C in the dark until ICP‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Collect hookah water
steps.instruction: During tobacco burning, capture the water vapor from the hookah into acid‑washed polypropylene tubes; repeat the collection three times for each sample.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards
steps.instruction:
Obtain two multi‑element standard solutions (10 ppm, 26XSM80B.5 L and 26XSM90C.5 L, MBH, London) containing the following elements:
- Solution 1: Al, As, Ba, Bi, Ca, Cd, Ce, Hg, Mg, Na, P, Pb, Se, Sr, Tb, Zn
- Solution 2: B, Co, Cr, Cu, Fe, K, Li, Mn, Mo, Ni, Sb, Si, Sn, Ti, V, Zn
Mix the two solutions and dilute daily to the desired concentrations for calibration curves.

steps.title: Set up ICP‑MS instrument
steps.instruction: Configure the Agilent 7900 ICP‑MS with octupole reaction system (ORS) in helium collision mode (He flow 4.2 mL min⁻¹) to remove matrix polyatomic interferences. Set instrumental parameters as follows: Power 1.5 kW, Plasma flow 15 L min⁻¹, Auxiliary flow 1.5 L min⁻¹, Nebulizer flow 0.7 L min⁻¹, Integration time 0.3 s per point, Stabilization delay 30 s, Replicates = 3. Use a Micro Mist glass concentric nebulizer, quartz double‑pass Scott‑type spray chamber at 4 °C, and a standard quartz torch (2.5 mm ID). Auto‑tune with Mass Hunter software and employ the Agilent I‑AS autosampler. Ensure all glassware and labware are acid‑washed and rinsed with ultra‑pure water (Milli‑Q).

steps.title: Analyze samples by ICP‑MS
steps.instruction:
Introduce each diluted digested sample and each reagent blank into the ICP‑MS using the single set of operating conditions (no cell‑gas mode switching). steps.title: Statistical data analysis
steps.instruction: Export the ICP‑MS results to Microsoft Excel 2019 for plotting. Because only three observations per group are available, apply non‑parametric tests. Perform paired comparisons of raw tobacco versus ash using the Friedman test in SPSS 21 (significance threshold P = 0.05; observed Friedman test P‑value = 0.10). Interpret the results accordingly.
